reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: Tally offers a no-code, document-style online form builder that could let me create or replace an intake form and send its submissions as JSON into the rest of an automation.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: The profile establishes that I manage an intake form that starts an automation, so the premise about a form being the “front door to a bigger workflow” fits directly. The email additionally assumes I may be building or willing to replace that form; whether the current form is painful, inadequate, or due for replacement is unknown.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: I deal with an intake form that feeds a larger automation.
Profile-supported: ownership of that automation is unclear or absent.
Email-only: I am currently putting together or revisiting the workflow.
Email-only: webhooks posting JSON are compatible with whatever receives submissions downstream.
Email-only: the listed field and block types cover my real intake requirements.
reader_verdicts.problem_now: The intake-to-automation handoff is relevant to my responsibilities, and unclear ownership makes ease of maintenance matter. But the profile does not establish that the current form is failing, that I need a replacement now, or that a new workflow is scheduled, so urgency is unknown.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: I understand how to try it, but I do not yet have a reason to interrupt my morning and replace or recreate an intake form I already manage; the email does not identify a concrete limitation it would remove from my current setup.
reader_verdicts.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had told me one concrete way I could test Tally against an existing intake workflow without rebuilding the whole form or disturbing the current automation.

Cut “Build the questions in plain sight, then shape what gets collected before anything moves downstream.” It restates the basic form-building idea without showing why I should reconsider my current intake.

Rewrite “When you want to connect it, webhooks are available free to all Tally users and can POST each submission as JSON to another app or URL” to add the practical test detail I need: whether I can inspect a sample payload and retry or diagnose a failed delivery before connecting a live automation.
Rewrite “decide whether it fits the workflow you’re putting together” so it does not assume I am building a new workflow; address someone evaluating an existing intake form too.

emails.subject: Meet Tally, the document-like form builder
emails.preview_text: Build forms by typing questions and adding the blocks you need.
emails.headline: Build the form your workflow starts with
emails.body:
Tally is officially here: an online form builder that works like a document. Type questions directly on the page, then add blocks for contact details, payments, signatures, file uploads, ratings, and more—without writing code.

That makes it useful when a form is the front door to a bigger workflow. Build the questions in plain sight, then shape what gets collected before anything moves downstream.

When you want to connect it, webhooks are available free to all Tally users and can POST each submission as JSON to another app or URL. Unlimited forms and submissions are free too, within fair usage guidelines.

Start with one real intake. You can create the form without signing up, see how the builder feels, and decide whether it fits the workflow you’re putting together.
